title: The Human Skeletal System
text: The human skeleton consists of 206 bones in adults, providing structural support, protecting internal organs, enabling movement through attachment of muscles, producing blood cells (in bone marrow), and storing minerals (especially calcium and phosphorus). The skeleton is divided into the axial skeleton (skull, vertebral column, and rib cage, 80 bones) and the appendicular skeleton (limbs and girdles, 126 bones). Bones are living tissue, constantly remodeled by osteoblasts (bone-forming cells) and osteoclasts (bone-resorbing cells). Calcium and vitamin D are essential for bone health. Osteoporosis is a disease of reduced bone density and increased fracture risk, particularly common in postmenopausal women.
